skill.name: auth-integration
skill.description: Guide for implementing Better Auth or NextAuth authentication in Next.js apps, including forms, sessions, protected routes, roles, and security checks.
skill.summary: Implement Next.js authentication flows with forms, session state, protected routes, and role checks.
skill.author: Awais68

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, TypeScript template literals, documentation links, and environment variable examples. No prompt injection, malicious command execution, filesystem access, credential exfiltration, or unsafe network behavior was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Static scanners may misread Markdown code fences and template literals as shell execution.
remediation.suggestion: Keep code examples clearly fenced and avoid ambiguous backtick-heavy formatting where plain prose is enough.

remediation.issue: Environment variable examples can be mistaken for secret handling.
remediation.suggestion: Continue using placeholders only, and state that real secrets must never be committed or printed.

content.value_statement: Authentication work is easy to under-specify and hard to secure. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through forms, sessions, protected routes, and role checks.
actual_capabilities: Guides Better Auth or NextAuth setup for Next.js App Router projects.
Defines login, signup, forgot password, and email verification form patterns.
Shows session hydration with Zustand and Better Auth client calls.
Explains middleware and client guards for protected dashboard routes.
Provides role and permission guard examples for common ERP roles.
Includes security checklist items, rate limiting, and audit logging guidance.
limitations: It provides implementation guidance, not a drop-in authentication package.
It assumes a Next.js App Router project with compatible auth libraries.
Project-specific database schema, secrets, and providers still need review.
It does not replace a dedicated security review or penetration test.

use_cases.title: Add Auth To A New App
use_cases.description: Create a full authentication baseline with provider setup, form validation, session state, and route protection.

use_cases.title: Standardize Access Control
use_cases.description: Define roles, permissions, middleware checks, and reusable guards for teams building dashboards or ERP workflows.

use_cases.title: Review Auth Security Requirements
use_cases.description: Check an implementation against practical controls for cookies, rate limits, email verification, and audit logging.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Basic Auth
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Next.js app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the auth-integration skill to add Better Auth with email and Google login to my Next.js App Router project. Include required files, environment variables, and setup steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build Auth Forms
prompt_templates.scenario: Create user-facing login and signup flows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the auth-integration skill to build login, signup, and forgot password pages. Use React Hook Form, Zod validation, loading states, and accessible error messages.

prompt_templates.title: Protect Dashboard Routes
prompt_templates.scenario: Add route protection after auth is configured.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the auth-integration skill to protect my dashboard routes. Add middleware checks, a client auth guard, session hydration, and redirects for unauthenticated users.

prompt_templates.title: Design Role-Based Access
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced permissions design for a production app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the auth-integration skill to design role-based access control for admin, teacher, student, and parent users. Include server-side checks, permission helpers, audit logging, and test cases.

output_examples.input: Add authentication to a new dashboard app.
output: A file plan for auth routes, forms, session store, middleware, and guards.
A checklist for environment variables, email verification, secure cookies, and session expiration.
Implementation notes for Better Auth, Prisma, and Google OAuth setup.

output_examples.input: Create role checks for an education dashboard.
output: A role model for admin, teacher, student, and parent users.
Permission groups for common actions such as managing users and viewing class data.
Guidance for enforcing checks in middleware, server actions, and UI guards.

output_examples.input: Review my login flow for missing security controls.
output: A review list covering CSRF, secure cookies, rate limits, email verification, and audit logs.
Concrete remediation steps for weak password rules or missing server-side authorization.
Testing suggestions for login failures, logout cleanup, and protected route redirects.

best_practices: Keep secrets in environment variables and use placeholders in shared examples.
Enforce authorization on the server, even when client guards improve user experience.
Add rate limiting, audit logging, secure cookies, and email verification before production release.
anti_patterns: Do not rely only on client-side redirects to protect sensitive routes.
Do not hardcode OAuth secrets, database URLs, or auth secrets in source files.
Do not skip rate limiting for login, signup, or password reset endpoints.

faq.question: Which projects fit this skill?
faq.answer: It fits Next.js App Router projects that need Better Auth, NextAuth, forms, sessions, protected routes, or RBAC.

faq.question: Does it install an auth provider automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives implementation guidance and file patterns that an agent can apply in your project.

faq.question: Can it support Google OAuth?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes Google provider configuration and environment variable guidance for client ID and client secret.

faq.question: Does it cover role-based access control?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes role constants, permission helpers, middleware checks, and component guards.

faq.question: Is it safe for production use?
faq.answer: It includes production controls, but your final implementation still needs project-specific security review.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
